newsitem.title: USA: Widow sues Kunstler law partner for using his name.
newsitem.headline: Widow sues Kunstler law partner for using his name.

text.p: The widow of famed defence lawyer William Kunstler filed a lawsuit late on Wednesday in New York State Supreme Court asking that her husband's law partner, Ron Kuby, be barred from using the Kunstler name in his law practice.

In an affidavit prepared for the complaint, Kunstler's widow, Margaret Ratner, claims that the use of the Kunstler name by Kuby "is not only unauthorised by the Estate and unethical, but it is misleading to the public who will be confused into believing that Kuby is somehow currently affiliated with my late husband...which he is clearly not."
Ratner is also demanding that Kuby return Kunstler's personal papers and his historical files.
Kuby, who says he was forced out of Kunstler's New York City office by Ratner five months after Kunstler's death in September 1995, disputed Ratner's charges and demands.

"Despite Bill Kunstler's clear and repeated statements that I was his law partner, his widow today refuses to accept the fact of the partnership," Kuby said in a telephone interview on Wednesday night.

"Our law partnership was acknowledged by all and gainsaid by none while Bill was alive. Bill Kunstler and I thought we were partners," he said, adding that judges and clients also thought they were partners.

Kunstler was famous for defending radical causes. The law firm clients include the Chicago Seven, Martin Luther King Jr., comedian Lenny Bruce, and Moslem militant El Sayyid Nosair, accused of killing Rabbi Meir Kahane. The two lawyers also represented Sheikh Omar Abdel-Rahman, later convicted of conspiracy in the plot to blow up the United Nations and other New York City landmarks.
